speaker: Doctor
text: I see the previous notes, but I must rely on your current symptoms to diagnose you. You mentioned shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after a tympanoplasty; can you tell me exactly when these symptoms started and if the pain is localized to the ear canal or deep inside the ear?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cholesteatoma recurrence. The combination of post-tympanoplasty history, shooting ear pain, and specifically pain when wearing earrings (indicating canal wall erosion or pressure on the prosthesis) is highly characteristic of this condition.
